title: Petrus Resources Announces Second Quarter 2026 Financial and Operating Results
article:
Petrus Resources Ltd. (TSX: PRQ) announced its financial and operating results for the second quarter of 2026, covering the period from April 1 to June 30. The Canadian exploration and development firm, headquartered in Calgary, Alberta, reported a notable uptick in both revenue and net income, reflecting stronger commodity prices and efficient cost management.

Total revenue reached CAD 120.4 million, up 12% year‑on‑year, driven largely by higher natural gas prices. Net income for the quarter was CAD 30.7 million, a 9% increase compared with Q2 2025, giving a per‑share earnings of CAD 0.45.

Operating net income climbed to CAD 25.3 million, representing a 15% rise from the same period last year. Exploration and development costs were controlled at CAD 10.1 million, a 3% reduction from Q2 2025, thanks to disciplined spending and a focus on high‑return projects.

Production volumes stabilized at 48,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day, a 2% increase over Q1 2026. The company also announced a new discovery that added 200 million barrels of recoverable reserves to its portfolio, reinforcing its long‑term asset base.

Market volatility in the energy sector, coupled with a stronger Canadian dollar, contributed to fluctuations in revenue, yet Petrus maintained profitability through hedging strategies and cost‑efficiency initiatives.

Chief Executive Officer Sarah McLeod highlighted the company's strategic focus on sustainable development and expressed confidence that the current growth trajectory would continue into the final quarter of the year.

Looking ahead, Petrus expects Q3 2026 to mirror its Q2 performance, with guidance for a full‑year net income of CAD 110–115 million. The firm plans to allocate a portion of cash flow to share repurchases and a modest dividend increase.

Investors have responded positively, with PRQ shares up 4.2% in after‑hours trading following the announcement. The company’s solid financial footing and expanding reserve base suggest a resilient outlook amid an uncertain macroeconomic environment.

Market volatility and a stronger Canadian dollar impacted revenue fluctuations, yet hedging and cost controls maintained profitability. The company plans cash flow allocation to share repurchases and a modest dividend increase. Investors reacted favorably, with shares up 4.2% after the announcement. The results reinforce Petrus’s resilience in a volatile energy market and strengthen its long‑term asset base. The company’s disciplined cost management and reserve expansion position it well for future earnings. Market participants view Petrus as a solid performer amid macroeconomic uncertainty. The announcement underscores the company’s strategic focus on growth and shareholder value. Petrus’s financial health and reserve growth support its ability to navigate commodity price swings. The company’s guidance reflects confidence in sustaining Q2 performance into the final quarter. Overall, Petrus Resources presents a positive outlook for investors seeking exposure to the Canadian energy sector.
